title: fix(plugin-form): record:line_items stops requiring childObject, so the page compile accepts a dataSource-bound node (objectui#11569)
body:
Fixes #11569
Clause-②: yes

## What changes

The `record:line_items` registration in `@object-ui/plugin-form` no longer declares `childObject` with `required: true`. The input now publishes a `description`: the node's `dataSource` binding can name the object instead (`dataSource.object` lands on this key and outranks an authored value), and a node with neither shows the panel's configuration hint and loads nothing.

Why: `@objectstack/spec` 17.6.0's `ComponentPropsMap['record:line_items']` leaves `childObject` optional "because the component-level `dataSource` binding can supply the object instead", and the renderer agrees (`RECORD_LINE_ITEMS_DATA_SOURCE` maps the binding's `object` onto `childObject`). The page compile (`compile()` in `@object-ui/sdui-parser`, whose `ok` is the save gate) reads the registration, so it refused a bound node that the row, the zod faces and the runtime all accept.

## The vocabulary question, measured

The manifest has no "one of these is required" form, so per the triage ruling `required: true` is dropped and nothing is added:

- `ComponentInput` (`@object-ui/types`, `base.ts`) declares `name`, `type`, `of`, `required` (a boolean), `enum` and `description`, plus retirement tombstones.
- `ManifestInput` (`@object-ui/sdui-parser`, `types.ts`) adds the framework-set `binding: 'object'` marker. It says an input NAMES an object and carries no requiredness.
- `validateTree`'s only requiredness check is `input.required && !(input.name in node)`.

`packages/types` is not edited. The same shape already landed in this repo: `element:number`'s `object` (objectui#10909), and the `objectName` inputs of `object-calendar`, `object-gantt`, `object-map` and `object-timeline`, each dropped `required` and gained a description that names the binding.

## Accept-set changes (for the contract review)

Measured against the manifest the console ships (`buildArtifacts` over `dev/manifest-registry.ts`). "Before" is this head with `required: true` put back through `ablation-replace.mjs`; "after" is this head.

| node | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `record:line_items` with `dataSource.object`, `relationshipField`, `columns`, no `childObject` | `ok: false`: one error, `missing-required-prop` naming `childObject` | `ok: true`, no diagnostics. The `dataSource` binding site is recorded in both runs |
| `record:line_items` with `relationshipField` and `columns`, and neither `childObject` nor `dataSource` | `ok: false`: the same error | `ok: true`, no diagnostics. The ruling leaves this node to the runtime: the panel shows the configuration hint naming `childObject` and fetches nothing. `LineItemsPanel.childObjectDecline.test.tsx` pins the hint, unchanged and green |
| `record:line_items` with `childObject`, `relationshipField` and `columns` | `ok: true` | `ok: true` (control) |

Generated artifacts that move with it (same generator, same runs):

- `sdui.manifest.json`, entry `record:line_items`, input `childObject`: `required: true` removed, `description` added.
- `sdui-intrinsics.d.ts` (the typed JSX face): `childObject: string` becomes `childObject?: string`.
- `sdui-blocks.md`, the required-props column for `record:line_items`: `childObject, relationshipField, columns` becomes `relationshipField, columns`.

Unchanged: `relationshipField` and `columns` stay required. The zod faces (`objectui validate`), the spec row and the renderer are not touched.

## registry-inputs-spec-parity

`apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts` does not compare requiredness, so nothing in it records this difference and the file is unchanged. Evidence: the file never reads an input's `required`, and it does read `input.of` and `input.type` (the control). It is green on this head.

## Pins

New: `apps/console/src/__tests__/line-items-bound-child-object-11569.test.ts`. It judges against the shipped `sdui.manifest.json` (written by `emitSduiManifest` and read back):

1. The published entry declares `childObject` as not required, with a description that names `dataSource` and `dataSource.object`. `relationshipField` and `columns` stay required.
2. The bound node compiles `ok` with no diagnostic, and the binding is recorded.
3. Control: the `childObject` node compiles `ok`.
4. Control: a node that names `childObject` but has no `relationshipField` is refused with exactly one `missing-required-prop`. This row reads the same before and after the fix.
5. The neither node draws no compile diagnostic about `childObject`.

Reproduced first: before the fix, rows 1, 2 and 5 were red, each with `missing-required-prop` naming `childObject` at error severity.

Ablation, run on the committed fix: `ablation-replace.mjs` put `required: true` back (anchor hit once, blob `e9b208727dd7` became `2591aef44b45`). Rows 1, 2 and 5 turned red (3 failed, 2 passed). The restore is proven by blob hash: `e9b208727dd7` equals HEAD and `git diff HEAD` is empty. On resolution: the console project aliases `@object-ui/plugin-form` to `packages/plugin-form/src`, so the mutation reaches the test without a build. One first attempt was refused by the tool before any test ran, because its replacement contained its own anchor. It restored to HEAD and measured nothing.

## Other edits

- `LineItemsPanel.tsx` and `LineItemsPanel.childObjectDecline.test.tsx`: comment-only. Two comments said `childObject` was declared `required: true` on the registry entry and that the block had no spec schema. They now state the current facts.
- `content/docs/guide/data-source.md`: one prose sentence, no code fence. A bound `record:line_items` node needs no `childObject` and the page compile accepts it. A node with neither shows the configuration hint.
- `.changeset/11569-line-items-child-object-optional.md`: `@object-ui/plugin-form` `minor`. A `Clause-②: yes` widening takes at least `minor`, which matches the objectui#10909 landing (PR objectui#10944). It was first graded `patch` and regraded at `84ee3be` after the at-tier contract review `5978497549`. Its widening paragraph opens with the `**Clause-②: yes (widening)**` banner.

## Acceptance notes

- `LineItemsPanelSchema.childObject` (the panel component's TypeScript prop type) is still `string`, not optional. It is a React prop type, not stored metadata: the gate fills it before the panel reads it, and the panel guards the `undefined` case. Recorded only. Carrier: none.
- The same defect class on sibling gate-wrapped blocks is listed in the dev report for the seat to file. Not touched here.
